preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(x) <= 5 * 10**5 for line in stdin.splitlines() for x in line.split() if x.isdigit())
preconditions.description: All integers in input are within the bounds 1 ≤ n, m, u, v ≤ 5⋅10^5, and u ≠ v for each edge.
Input consists of exactly m + 1 lines: first line with n and m, followed by m edge lines.

preconditions.expression: all(u != v for u, v in (line.split() for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:]))
preconditions.description: Each edge connects distinct nodes (u ≠ v).

preconditions.expression: len({u for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:] for u in line.split()}) == n
preconditions.description: The graph is connected (all nodes are reachable from any other node).
No duplicate edges exist (each pair of nodes is connected by at most one edge).

preconditions.expression: len({(u, v) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:] for u, v in [tuple(sorted(line.split()))]}) == m
preconditions.description: No duplicate edges exist (each pair of nodes is connected by at most one edge, undirected).

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip().split() == [str(max_distance) for max_distance in compute_max_distances(n, edges)]
postconditions.description: For each node i (1 ≤ i ≤ n), the i-th output integer is the maximum distance from node i to any leaf in the tree obtained by removing edges to minimize this distance. The tree is formed by removing edges such that the graph becomes acyclic and connected, and the maximum distance from node i to any leaf is minimized.
Output contains exactly n space-separated integers, one for each node.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(x) <= n for x in stdout.strip().split())
postconditions.description: Each output integer is a valid node index (1 ≤ output ≤ n).
